Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sachin Khilari wins gold as India sweep all three shot put medals
Article Text:
Sachin Khilari (Image credit: X)

Khilari defends his gold

What is the F46 category?

India won all three medals in the men’s shot put F46 event at the Asian Para Games on Wednesday, with Sachin Sarjerao Khilari taking gold with a Games record.Khilari, a silver medallist at the Paris Paralympics, defended the gold he had won at the previous edition of the Games in China. He produced his best throw of 15.87m with his sixth and final attempt to set a new Games record.The earlier record was 15.67m.Mohd. Yasser won silver with a throw of 15.06m in the third round, while Parveen took bronze with 14.94m.Khilari saved his best effort for his final throw, going past the previous Games record to finish on top of the podium.His victory helped India secure all three medals in the event, with Yasser and Parveen finishing second and third.The F46 category is for field athletes who have an amputation above or below the elbow on one arm, or a similar upper-limb impairment.Athletes compete in a standing position and use their hips and legs to generate power for their throws.
Article Summary: Sachin Sarjerao Khilari won gold with a Games record throw of 15.87m. He defended the gold he had won at the previous edition of the Games in China. India won all three medals in the event, with Yasser and Parveen finishing second and third.

Article Title: Three titles, 15 wins: Khushi Kadian makes her mark at Fenesta
Article Text:
Haryana’s Khushi Kadian

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: There was a time when losing a tennis match left Khushi Kadian in tears and questioning her future in the sport. At 13, the Rohtak girl is learning to turn setbacks into stepping stones. Her stunning triple crown at the Fenesta Open National Tennis Championship earlier this week offered the latest evidence of that transformation.“There were so many times when I wanted to give up tennis. But I told myself that I had worked so hard and had to do something," she told TOI.Across a gruelling week, Khushi won 15 consecutive matches to sweep the girls’ under-14 singles, under-16 singles and under-16 doubles titles, partnering Sanmitha Harini. She beat Siddhi Pandey 6-3, 6-2 in the under-14 final before outlasting Ranjhana Sangram 7-6 (7-3), 7-5 in a demanding under-16 singles decider. She then teamed up with Harini to clinch the doubles crown, defeating Purvi Patwa and Sangram 6-3, 6-3.The triumph was especially significant after a disappointing outing in Thailand, where she lost to China’s Li Xiaoke in the quarterfinals of the girls’ singles at the GSPDP Asian 14U Junior Championships.There were familiar thoughts of quitting, but Khushi chose to regroup.“I really wanted to win the Nationals this time, and I am happy about it,” she said, crediting her parents and coaches for their unwavering support. "One thing I have learnt and always say is, 'come on, this is your point'. And especially on my serves, I get a bit more confident that, 'yes, this is your serve and you are going to hit an ace'. I am becoming mature and understanding my game well."Once prone to tears after early-round defeats, Khushi now speaks of staying present, breathing between points and playing one point at a time. A fan of Elena Rybakina, she hopes to progress to junior Grand Slams before pursuing her bigger ambition.“I really want to do well at the Australian Open at one point of my career,” she said. “You just have to be patient, work hard and give your best, whether you win or lose.”
Article Summary: Haryana's Khushi Kadian wins triple crown at Fenesta Open National Tennis Championship. The 13-year-old won 15 consecutive matches to sweep the girls’ under-14 singles, under-16 singles and under- 16 doubles titles.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Nishad Kumar leads India’s 14-medal athletics haul with double gold
Article Text:
India's Nishad Kumar (AP/PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s track and field athletes turned grit into glory on Tuesday, collecting five gold, four silver and five bronze medals at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya to take their athletics tally to 20.The 14-medal haul featured record-breaking performances, emotional comebacks and podium sweeps, proof that determination can outpace the toughest odds. Nishad Kumar stood tallest, literally and figuratively. The Himachal Pradesh high jumper cleared 2.04m to win the men’s T47 gold with a Games record, adding to the long jump title he claimed on Monday. He became only the third Indian to win two gold medals at a single Asian Para Games, joining runner Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi. T47 is for athletes with upper-limb impairments.Deepthi Jeevanji launched India’s gold rush by defending her women’s 400m T20 crown in a Games-record 56.36 seconds. The 23-year-old from Telangana, who has an intellectual impairment, is also a world champion and Paralympic bronze medallist. Raised by small-farmer parents in a village in Warangal, she pursued running despite social taunts directed at her family for supporting her ambitions.A school physical education teacher first spotted her talent; later, coach N Ramesh and badminton coach Pullela Gopichand helped her journey gather pace.Simran claimed her maiden Para Games gold in the women’s 200m T12, clocking a record 24.80 seconds. The sprinter, who has a moderate visual impairment, is rebuilding with guide Shivam after her previous guide, Umar Saifi, was banned for a doping violation. Debutant Tejalben Damor took bronze in 25.23 seconds, drawing confidence from the medal despite her family’s financial struggles.In the men’s combined F51/52/53 discus, Pranav Soorma won gold with an Asian record of 11.66m, while fellow F51 athlete Ram Ratan Singh secured silver with 10.35m. The seated F51 classification involves significant movement limitations in the trunk, legs and hands. Placings in combined classes use the Raza points system, which enables fair comparisons between athletes with different levels of impairment.Devender Kumar completed another Indian gold in the men’s F44/64 discus, throwing 49.71m. Rakesh won silver and Pardeep Kumar bronze, giving India all three medals. F44 athletes compete without a prosthesis, while F64 athletes use one.India’s other silver medals came through Preeti Pal in the women’s 200m T35 and Pradeep Kumar in the men’s javelin F53/54, where his personal-best throw of 27.45m earned him second place. Ayush Verma added bronze in the same event.Bronze medals also went to Praveen Sharma in the men’s shot put F11 and Hokato Hotozhe Sema in the men’s shot put F56/57 events.
Article Summary: India claim five gold, four silver and five bronze medals at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The 14-medal haul featured record-breaking performances, emotional comebacks and podium sweeps. Deepthi Jeevanji defended her women’s 400m T20 crown in a Games-record 56.36 seconds. Devender Kumar completed another Indian gold in the men's F44/64 discus.

Article Title: EFI administrator seeks Rs 25 lakh in damages, serves defamation notice on Hangzhou Asiad gold medallist Chheda
Article Text:
India’s Hriday Vipul Chheda (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: In a bizarre turn of events, Lt Col Sandeep Dewan, member (administration) of the ad hoc committee governing the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), has served a defamation notice on Hangzhou Asian Games gold medallist Hriday Chheda, demanding Rs 25 lakh in damages and an unconditional apology over allegations concerning the handling of the Indian dressage team ahead of and during the recently concluded Aichi-Nagoya multisport continental event.The six-page legal notice, dated October 17 and in possession of TOI, also seeks the withdrawal and deletion of Chheda’s September 8 email to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and sports officials, in which the rider alleged that the veterinary report declaring his horse, Dono Di Maggio, unfit was engineered to clear the way for reserve Anush Agarwalla. Chheda accused Dewan of collusion, fraud and concealment, questioning the attempt to jeopardise his participation in the Asian Games.The development raises questions over the priorities of an administrator appointed to restore order in a federation long plagued by governance controversies, internal power struggles and selection disputes. Instead of addressing an athlete’s grievances, the administrator is now seeking damages from one of India’s leading riders for raising concerns about his conduct.For the record, Chheda’s horse, Dono Di Maggio, was subsequently cleared by the Games organisers to compete in Japan.The horse was the best-performing among the Indian riders in Aichi-Nagoya.After being served the notice, Chheda expressed deep anguish over the way he had been treated and wrote a strongly worded email to IOA president P T Usha."The vindictiveness, high-handedness and arrogance is apparent from the attached legal notice. The irony is appalling: an athlete who faced harassment and an attempt to prevent his participation and subsequently demonstrated through his horse’s performances that he was fit to compete, is now facing legal threats from the very person whose conduct he questioned," Chheda wrote to Usha. The email is in possession of TOI."An administration that resorts to legal threats against athletes rather than welcoming scrutiny of its own conduct has no place in sporting governance. Individuals such as Col Dewan must be held accountable for their conduct and questioned on their suitability to hold positions of responsibility in Indian sport," Chheda said."Meanwhile, athletes have received no meaningful support from the Federation and continue to bear the consequences of its failures. The multiple legal disputes concerning the Federation’s functioning, along with the reported suspension by the international governing body, FEI, have further jeopardised athletes’ careers and international participation," he added.Dewan’s notice, however, disputed the allegations, maintaining that the veterinary examination covered all Indian team horses and that the decision on a late replacement rested with the IOA, not with him individually. It stated that the September 8 email falsely accused him of fraud, collusion and concealment, thereby damaging his reputation."The impugned email has gravely harmed my client's reputation as a veteran Army officer, as a sports administrator and as Team Leader. It has exposed him to suspicion and ridicule among the very persons with whom he must work and caused him severe mental distress," Dewan's lawyer, Aroon Menon, stated in the notice issued on his client's behalf."By making and publishing the impugned email, you have committed the offence of defamation under Section 356(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, punishable under Section 356(2). My client is the person aggrieved and is entitled to file a complaint under Section 222 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Your acts also constitute the civil wrong of libel, for which my client is entitled to sue you for damages, a mandatory injunction directing retraction and a permanent injunction restraining further publication," the lawyer stated."You are therefore called upon within 7 (seven) days of receipt of this notice to: (i) Unconditionally withdraw the impugned email and every imputation in it against my client; (ii) Tender an unconditional written apology to my client, sent by email from hridaychheda98@gmail.com to every recipient of the impugned email, with a copy to the undersigned; (iii) Delete the impugned email and refrain from forwarding, circulating or repeating it or any similar imputation, in any medium, including email, messaging apps, social media and the press; (iv) Pay an amount of Rs 25,00,000 (twenty-five lakh) as compensation to my client for the harm to his reputation and the mental distress caused, and Rs 50,000 (fifty thousand) towards the costs of the present notice," the notice added.
Article Summary: Lt Col Sandeep Dewan served a defamation notice on Hriday Chheda. Dewan is a member of the ad hoc committee governing the Equestrian Federation of India. He is demanding Rs 25 lakh in damages and an unconditional apology. The six-page legal notice, dated October 17, is in possession of TOI.

Article Title: Temba Bavuma enters record books with captain’s knock as South Africa produce great fightback
Article Text:
South Africa's captain Temba Bavuma (AP/PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma produced a record-breaking innings against Australia, registering his highest Test score and helping his side recover from a precarious position to post a formidable total on Day 3 of the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha on Tuesday.Bavuma's 179 is the fourth-highest individual score by a South African captain in a home Test, behind Hashim Amla's 208 against West Indies in Centurion in 2014, Amla's 201 against England in Cape Town in 2016 and Graeme Smith 's 183 against England in Cape Town in 2010.The knock also ranks as the second-highest Test score at Gqeberha, behind Herschelle Gibbs' 196 against India in 2001.Bavuma's innings proved crucial after South Africa slumped to 110-6, putting the hosts in danger of surrendering control of the contest. The skipper held the innings together, batting for 334 deliveries and striking 18 fours and a six as South Africa declared at 425-9.The recovery was among the most remarkable in Test cricket. South Africa's total was the second-highest innings score by a team after losing six wickets for 110 runs or fewer, behind England's 446 against Pakistan at Lord's in 2010, when they had been reduced to 102-7.Bavuma had walked in at 12-2 on the opening day and remained at the crease as South Africa slipped to 92-5 amid rain and a wet outfield on the following day.His patience and composure proved decisive as the lower order rallied around him. Marco Jansen provided the first major support, adding 132 runs with Bavuma for the seventh wicket. Jansen scored 85 before being dismissed by Scott Boland, who finished with figures of 5-81.Simon Harmer then joined his captain and the pair put together a decisive 183-run partnership for the eighth wicket. Harmer contributed 82, his maiden Test half-century, to help swing the contest in South Africa's favour.Bavuma reached his fifth Test century off 226 balls before accelerating to surpass his previous best of 172 against West Indies in Johannesburg in 2023. His innings ended when Mitchell Starc dismissed him, with South Africa declaring soon afterwards.Australia faced a difficult finish to the day, losing Nic Maddinson for a four-ball duck to Kagiso Rabada. The visitors were 3-1 at stumps.Australia won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0. South Africa, the reigning World Test champions, are looking to respond as both sides target a place in the 2027 World Test Championship final.
Article Summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma scored his highest Test score. Bavuma's 179 is the fourth-highest individual score by a South African captain in a home Test, behind Hashim Amla's 208 against West Indies in Centurion in 2014 and Graeme Smith's 183 against England in Cape Town in 2010. South Africa declared at 425-9 on Day 3 of the second Test.

Article Title: No sponsor, a career-threatening setback and one big dream: Nayanika Sanga’s story
Article Text:
Nayanika Sanga (Insta)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Nayanika Sanga, golf has always been about more than the scorecard. As the 22-year-old from Gurugram prepares to compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, she is drawing on lessons learnt over years of competition, international exposure and a difficult comeback from injury. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.The philosophy reflects a maturity that has developed through experience. Having travelled abroad for tournaments, including competing in France, Nayanika has learnt to approach the demands of professional golf with greater perspective.“When you play in India, it is like a family. You feel at home and at ease. But when you play outside, the environment is different. People are new, and there can be a language barrier. I think that has made me a little more resilient. When I compete back home now, I feel comfortable because I know the place and the people,” she said.Her journey began when she was five. Her father, who serves in the Navy, wanted her to take up a sport, believing it would help her develop as an individual. She tried squash, tennis and golf, but the response to her natural ability with a club encouraged the family to pursue the latter.Competition soon followed, and the game became a defining part of her life.One of the earliest milestones arrived when she was 11, winning the Kazi Cup at Willingdon Club in Mumbai.“That was definitely a life-changing experience because that was my first win as a child, a big win as a child. Once you start winning, it reinforces that feeling that you want to keep chasing it again and again,” she said.The road since then, however, has not been without setbacks. A wrist injury four years ago came at a particularly difficult time, when she had just turned professional and was playing well. Gratitude journalling became an important part of that process.“When I started playing again, I began focusing on smaller things and feeling grateful that at least today I can play, and tomorrow I can compete. Instead of thinking, ‘I need to win today’, being grateful for the small things in life has definitely helped me,” she said.Physical conditioning has also played a significant role in her return. A professional golfer’s workload extends beyond the hours spent practising and playing. Frequent travel, tournaments scheduled close together and the physical demands of carrying her own bag at overseas events can take a toll. Nayanika credits her strength and conditioning coach, Shaurya Sinha, with helping her rebuild confidence in her body and handle the demands of the circuit.“Because of fitness, I have been a little more resilient to injuries. Other than the injury I had four years ago, I have not had any issues, and I feel my fitness routine is what gets me going every week,” she said.The Women’s Indian Open will present another test. Nayanika regards the DLF Golf and Country Club course as challenging, but prefers to see its demands as an opportunity rather than an obstacle.“I think it is challenging in a fun way. I do not see the course as challenging; rather, every day will be a new challenge there. It will be fun to tackle a new challenge every day,” she said.That outlook also shapes how she approaches a field featuring accomplished players. Rather than becoming preoccupied with the reputations of her opponents, she wants to learn from them while remaining focused on her own performance. She relies more on feel and instinct than data when making decisions on the course, trusting her judgement when she believes her game is in good shape.Nayanika has also witnessed the growth of women’s golf in India. When she first turned professional, she recalled fields of around 30 to 35 players. This year, she said, the numbers have risen to approximately 60 to 62, reflecting greater interest among younger golfers in pursuing the professional route. Lower scores and more opportunities to compete overseas have contributed to the improving standard.Yet the growth of the game has not removed one of its persistent challenges: funding. Despite competing abroad and continuing to develop as a professional, she is still looking for a sponsor. Coming from a middle-class family, with her father serving in the Navy, she knows the financial demands of sustaining a career on tour.“It has been tough. My parents have sacrificed so much for me, and they continue to do so to support me,” she said.Her grandparents also travelled with her to tournaments when she was younger, stepping in whenever her father’s work commitments prevented him from accompanying her. Nayanika acknowledges their contribution.Away from golf, time with friends and playing badminton help her switch off from the constant demands of professional competition. She also looks up to Diksha Dagar and Aditi Ashok whose achievements have out Indian golf on the global map.Nayanika hopes her journey can encourage more young girls to pursue sport, particularly in a society where conventional career choices often dominate expectations.“If you fall in love with a sport, there is nothing better than that feeling. Parents should be willing to explore sporting opportunities when their children show interest and ability,” she said.As she heads into the Women’s Indian Open, her ambitions remain tied to the fundamentals she has learnt through experience: trust her instincts, stay patient and focus on the next shot. For a golfer who has learnt to find perspective in adversity, the challenge is not simply to compete against a strong field, but to keep moving forward, one round at a time.
Article Summary: Nayanika Sanga, 22, will compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.

Article Title: Three Jharkhand players in India squad for historic lawn bowls series against New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Sunil Bahadur, Dinesh Kumar and Reshma Kumari

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov, part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two countries.Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme.2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallists Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, have been selected alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh for the series, scheduled from Nov 16-18 in Auckland.“This is a very important event for us because only four sports are taking part in the centenary celebrations. On the days we are playing, no other sport will be taking place, which means we will receive exclusive coverage,” Bowling Federation of India president Ravi Bengani told TOI in an exclusive interview on Thursday.India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches — men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2.The New Zealand series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.A 12-member Indian contingent will travel to Malaysia later this month for a World Bowls-sanctioned tournament, while another group will compete in an invitational event in Hong Kong, where Indian players won bronze medals last year.The federation’s confidence has also received a boost from Putul Sonowal’s recent podium finish at the Champion of Champions event, a first for an Indian player at the prestigious competition.“We have decided to participate in as many World Bowls-sanctioned events as possible. International exposure is crucial if we want to bridge the gap with the leading nations,” Bengani said.The federation is also planning to strengthen its support structure through its partnership with Bowls New Zealand. Bengani revealed that India currently does not have a dedicated national coach, making the proposed knowledge-sharing programme particularly significant.“We have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand and now we will have more exchange programmes. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani said.The plans have gained momentum following the federation’s recognition by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports earlier this year, a move expected to improve funding and access to high-performance support.As far as the 2030 Commonwealth Games are concerned, the federation has set ambitious targets. “I’m committing to at least four gold medals for India in 2030. Personally, I feel we can win even more if we continue on the current path,” Bengani said.With a packed international calendar, plans to bring in New Zealand coaches and technical experts, and Ahmedabad 2030 on the horizon, the federation believes Indian lawn bowls is entering its most ambitious phase yet.
Article Summary: Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme. India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches. The series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.

Article Title: EFI mess costs Indian riders global stage, FEI ban from Dec 1
Article Text:
Equestrian Federation of India

New Delhi:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India will negatively impact athletes' futures? Yes, definitely No, it won't 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price. Caught in a prolonged governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes’ exposure to global competition.The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections, effectively shutting Indian riders, officials, trainers and horses out of international events. TOI is in possession of FEI’s Oct 15 letter confirming the decision, which was taken at the international body's board meeting on Oct 13.Explaining its move, the FEI said the EFI’s prolonged governance crisis had reached a tipping point. “The absence of elections to date to elect a new Executive Committee, has resulted in a prolonged governance and leadership irregularity that is no longer sustainable,” the letter by FEI Governance Director Francisco Lima stated.The crisis follows the Delhi high court’s dissolution of the EFI executive committee in Feb 2026. Its elected tenure had expired in Sept 2023, while fresh elections remain pending nine months after the court’s intervention. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) constituted an ad hoc committee on March 27 to oversee the federation and facilitate the electoral process.While acknowledging the committee’s Sept 27 submission and its work, the FEI said elections were expected by Jan 31, 2027. However, the suspension will be reviewed only after the polls are held and evaluated by the international body.The consequences are sweeping. Citing its statutes, the FEI said the EFI “may not attend or be represented at any session or meeting of any FEI body, nor may it organise international events.” More damagingly, athletes, officials, trainers and horses “may not participate in international events organised by the FEI or any other national federation, whether under the Indian flag or the FEI flag.”With the suspension taking effect before the stated election deadline, Indian riders risk losing crucial international competition opportunities. Their return will depend on the completion of elections and the FEI’s subsequent evaluation, leaving athletes caught in a governance crisis they did not create.
Article Summary: The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections. Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes' exposure to global competition.

Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey.Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip.Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution.Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.

Article Title: 'We have plans for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi': New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner ahead of T20I series vs India
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AFP Photo)

New Zealand have plans for Sooryavanshi

Santner expects Bhuvneshwar to enjoy New Zealand conditions

Santner hopes bowlers will have their say

Santner backs India but expects a challenge

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could be a tough batter to stop if he gets a chance in India's playing XI for the five-match T20I series. The series begins on Thursday, and Santner said his team has already worked on plans to deal with the young left-hander.Sooryavanshi has not played regularly for India since being picked for the tour of the UK earlier this year. Regular openers Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been doing well, limiting his chances. However, Santner believes the 15-year-old has an important role to play for India, whether in this series or in the future.Santner said New Zealand have studied Sooryavanshi's aggressive batting, including his performances in the IPL. The Kiwi captain also pointed out that Indian batters faced short-pitched bowling during the England tour."He (Sooryavanshi) did not play in the last series (against West Indies), but we know how good he is, in IPL. We know other players like Abhishek are doing very well. But he (Sooryavanshi) has a huge part to play for India, whether it's in this series or not, but in future," Santner said at the pre-series press conference on Wednesday."If he does get a crack at this series, we've seen what he can do and guys have found it quite hard to stop him. I know in England, they went quite short and hard at a lot of the Indian batters. I think we've seen him in the IPL and how aggressive he can be. So we've got some plans for him if he happens to play."Santner also spoke about the return of veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar to India's T20I team after an absence of nearly four years.The New Zealand captain expects Bhuvneshwar to be effective in local conditions, especially with the new ball."I think Bhuvi will love these conditions in New Zealand. If there's anything in the wicket, he finds something out of it. On some flat ones in India, he still managed to nip the ball and swing the ball, so I think with the new ball out here, especially, it'll be a challenge (for New Zealand)."In India, it's pretty challenging as a bowler these days. We've seen in the recent series, 250 getting chased down. Who wants to be a bowler, but he (Bhuvneshwar) might like it out here a little bit better."Santner is hoping the series will give bowlers a chance to dominate, although he warned that conditions could change quickly."I hope so. I think maybe the first game it might be, but it can change pretty quickly. It's very weather dependent. The second game is a used pitch, same pitch we used for first game. It could be a bit flatter."If it nips around, we've got to play accordingly. If it's flat, you've got to play accordingly," said the 34-year-old left-arm spinner.Santner added that Indian batters have enough experience to handle different conditions around the world."If there is a little bit in it, you might have to change a few shots, but they've played on fast, bouncy wickets before. They've played all around the world and done really well. It's going to be a challenge this series and we're looking forward to it," he added.Santner acknowledged India's strength ahead of the series, while pointing out that conditions in New Zealand will be different from those at home."They (India) are a well-gelled team and playing some good cricket. We know the conditions will be a little bit different to what they've had at home. The pitches here will be a little bit bouncy. I guess there's still memories and a lot of this group were at the World Cup."And obviously the series beforehand where India beat us 4-1. So again, we know that they're a great team and have done it for a long time."Santner said the conditions could give New Zealand a slight advantage, but both teams will need contributions from their entire squads."We're going around the country, conditions can change. I think both teams are changing a little bit just with the schedule and the quick turnaround. So, it's going to be a full squad effort for both teams to put in some good performances."After the five-match T20I series, India and New Zealand will play a five-match ODI series, followed by two Tests.
Article Summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could be a tough batter to stop if he gets a chance in India's playing XI for the five-match T20I series. Santner said his team has already worked on plans to deal with the young left-hander. The series begins on Thursday.

Article Title: 'We were lacking that': Shreyas Iyer makes big admission as Bhuvneshwar Kumar returns

Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Shreyas Iyer (Agency Image)

Iyer anticipates pace challenge in New Zealand

India captain Shreyas Iyer is looking forward to having Bhuvneshwar Kumar back in the T20I setup, believing the veteran pacer's recent performances in the Indian Premier League ( IPL ) have demonstrated his ability to excel in the shortest format.Bhuvneshwar could return to international cricket in the five-match T20I series against New Zealand, with the first match scheduled to be played in Christchurch. The comeback would come nearly four years after his last appearance for India in the format, in November 2022.His anticipated return against the West Indies at home was washed out by rain recently, leaving fans waiting a little longer to see the experienced swing bowler back in Indian colours.Since his last T20I appearance, Bhuvneshwar has enjoyed a resurgence with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB), playing a key role in the franchise's back-to-back IPL title triumphs in 2025 and 2026. He has claimed 45 wickets in 31 matches during this period, averaging 22.55 at an economy rate of 8.52.His latest IPL campaign was particularly impressive. Bhuvneshwar finished as the tournament's second-highest wicket-taker, collecting 28 wickets in 16 matches at an average of 17.89 and an economy rate of 7.95.Speaking to reporters ahead of the opening T20I, Iyer highlighted the experience the 36-year-old would bring to an Indian bowling attack that has featured several new faces."He brings a lot of experience to the team. And we were lacking that. Especially after IPL. We had a lot of new bowlers. But in T20, if you see his career graph, he has won IPL in the last two years. So, he has a very good idea of dominating this format," Iyer said.Bhuvneshwar has taken 90 wickets in 87 T20Is for India at an average of 23.10. His record includes two five-wicket hauls and three four-wicket hauls.He is now 10 wickets away from becoming the fifth Indian bowler to claim 100 T20I wickets, joining Arshdeep Singh (145),Jasprit Bumrah (126), Hardik Pandya (114) and Axar Patel (113).The veteran pacer is also approaching another significant career milestone. With 294 international wickets across formats, he needs six more to reach 300, a mark achieved by only 13 Indian bowlers so far. Reaching the landmark would make him the 14th Indian bowler overall and the ninth fast bowler from the country to do so.Beyond Bhuvneshwar's return, Iyer expects India's batters to face a stern examination from New Zealand's pace-heavy attack. He stressed the importance of adapting quickly to the local conditions and using the practice sessions to develop a clear plan."If we look at the conditions here, fast bowling suits here. I have been here before, and it is not like the conditions are completely different. In England, the way we played, they had prepared the wickets according to our batting. But on a given day, no one knows how the wicket will be. So, we will try to acclimatise as soon as possible. And once we have a good practice session, every individual will get a fair idea of how to plan," he said.
Article Summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar could return to international cricket in the five-match T20I series against New Zealand. The comeback would come nearly four years after his last appearance for India in the format, in November 2022. Captain Shreyas Iyer believes the veteran pacer's recent performances in the Indian Premier League ( IPL ) have demonstrated his ability to excel in the shortest format.

Article Title: 'He can't walk in right now': Shreyas Iyer says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has 'more years to get opportunities'

India T20 captain Shreyas Iyer has made it clear that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait for regular opportunities in the playing XI, with established openers Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson continuing to deliver at the top of the order.Despite the teenager's impressive rise, Iyer believes there is no need to rush his integration into the side, pointing out that India's current opening combination has been performing consistently and played a key role in the team's successful defence of the T20 World Cup title earlier this year.Speaking on the eve of India's five-match T20I series against New Zealand, Iyer stressed that the 15-year-old has plenty of time to establish himself at the international level and should remain comfortable within the team environment while waiting for his opportunities."It's important that a talent like him (Sooryavanshi) should always be happy around the dressing room," Iyer said."He is very young, he has more years to get opportunities. It's not like he can walk in right now, because our openers are scoring consistently, and they have won the World Cup."Sooryavanshi was included in India's squads for the England and Ireland tours earlier this year. However, he has featured in only eight of the 21 T20Is India have played since then, with Abhishek and Samson largely retaining their places as the first-choice opening pair.The youngster was given an opportunity to open during the Asian Games, where Samson moved down to No. 3 to accommodate him at the top of the order.While Iyer does not expect Sooryavanshi to walk straight into the playing XI, he believes the experience of touring overseas and getting a feel for different conditions will benefit the youngster in the long run."So, if you see, when he is coming overseas, he will get a fair idea how to play on these particular wickets."Next time, whenever he comes in these conditions, he will be very well-prepared. And he can also instruct the other team members, whoever comes here for the first time."
Article Summary: India T20 captain Shreyas Iyer says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait for regular opportunities in the playing XI. Iyer stressed that the 15-year-old has plenty of time to establish himself at the international level and should remain comfortable within the team environment.

Australia captain Pat Cummins endured a difficult outing with the ball as South Africa mounted a remarkable recovery in the second Test at St George’s Park in Gqeberha, with his figures of 0/96 ranking as the second-most expensive wicketless return of his career.Cummins conceded 96 runs without taking a wicket, better only than his 0/101 against India in Sydney in 2019. The expensive spell came as South Africa recovered from 110-6 to declare at 425-9 on Day 3, putting Australia under pressure after a dramatic turnaround.South Africa’s lower order made the most of the opportunity after the hosts lost their sixth wicket early in the morning session. Captain Temba Bavuma led the fightback with a career-best 179, while Marco Jansen scored 85 and Simon Harmer contributed 82.The recovery was particularly significant in statistical terms. South Africa scored 315 runs after losing their sixth wicket, the second-highest such total in a Test innings. Their effort fell just short of the 318 runs they added against Australia at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in 2008.Australia have also conceded only one higher total after taking the sixth wicket: the 363 runs West Indies scored at Bridgetown in 1955.South Africa's 318-run effort in Melbourne in 2008 is the other entry ahead of the latest Gqeberha performance.The hosts had been in serious trouble at 110-6 after Wiaan Mulder fell for 13 to Mitchell Starc , who claimed his 450th Test wicket. Bavuma and Jansen initially steadied the innings with a 132-run seventh-wicket partnership before Jansen was dismissed by Scott Boland, who finished with 5-81.Harmer then joined Bavuma and the pair added 183 runs for the eighth wicket, turning the innings around. Harmer struck 10 fours and a six in his maiden Test half-century before being bowled by Marnus Labuschagne.Bavuma, meanwhile, reached his fifth Test century off 226 balls and went past his previous best of 172 against West Indies in Johannesburg in 2023. He eventually fell to Starc, bringing the innings to a close soon afterwards.Australia lost Nic Maddinson for a four-ball duck to Kagiso Rabada late in the day and were 3-1 at stumps.Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0.
Article Summary: Cummins conceded 96 runs without taking a wicket, better only than his 0/101 against India in Sydney in 2019. The expensive spell came as South Africa recovered from 110-6 to declare at 425-9 on Day 3. Captain Temba Bavuma led the fightback with a career-best 179. Marco Jansen scored 85 and Simon Harmer contributed 82.

Article Title: Harmanpreet Kaur unleashes six-hitting blitz as India thrash Zimbabwe by 92 runs to complete 3-0 T20I series sweep

Mayers fights back, but Zimbabwe fall short

India’s women turned Raipur into a six-hitting spectacle, with Shafali Verma and Harmanpreet Kaur unleashing a batting assault before Nandani Sharma’s three-wicket haul sealed a 92-run victory over Zimbabwe in the third T20I on Tuesday. The emphatic win completed a 3-0 series sweep for the Women in Blue, extended their winning streak in the format to 11 matches and handed them their biggest T20I victory by run margin on home soil.Shafali smashed 69 off 37 balls, while Harmanpreet rolled back the years with an unbeaten 91 off just 41 deliveries as India piled up 216/7 after opting to bat. Zimbabwe showed greater resistance than in their previous outings, with Sharne Mayers scoring a fighting 60, but Nandani’s 3/18 ensured the visitors finished at 124/7 in their 20 overs.India’s victory also marked Zimbabwe’s 23rd consecutive defeat in women’s T20Is, underlining the gulf between the sides despite a spirited individual effort from Mayers.With India already leading the series 2-0, Smriti Mandhana opted to bat first and used the opportunity to give the middle order more time in the middle. Anushka Sharma was promoted to open alongside Shafali, while Mandhana held herself back.The move paid dividends as the opening pair added 54 runs off just 32 balls.Anushka struck 28 off 20 deliveries, including a powerful six off Tendai Makusha in the fifth over, while Shafali continued her aggressive approach at the other end.The opener brought up her second consecutive half-century, peppering the leg-side boundary with a series of sixes over deep midwicket. She also used the sweep effectively against the spinners, ensuring Zimbabwe struggled to build pressure during the powerplay and middle overs.Shafali eventually departed for 69 off 37 balls, having provided India with the platform for another imposing total.Harmanpreet took charge after Shafali’s dismissal, producing a commanding innings that showcased her power-hitting at its best. The India captain struck an unbeaten 91 off 41 balls, including five sixes, as the hosts maintained their scoring momentum.The 37-year-old had struggled to find her rhythm on the slower surfaces during the Women’s Asia Cup and had limited opportunities to bat during India’s triumphant Asian Games campaign in Japan. Tuesday’s innings offered a timely reminder of her ability to dominate an attack when conditions favour stroke-making.India accelerated spectacularly at the death, plundering 62 runs in the final five overs despite losing four wickets. Their total of 216/7 left Zimbabwe facing a steep challenge.Zimbabwe’s chase suffered an immediate setback when Kelis Ndhlovu was dismissed for a first-ball duck. Mayers, however, refused to let the innings drift, counterattacking with a muscular knock that kept the visitors in the contest for a period.She scored 60 off 49 balls, striking four boundaries and four sixes, and found support from Beloved Biza as Zimbabwe attempted to rebuild after the early loss. Mayers’ innings was the standout contribution in a chase that otherwise lacked sustained partnerships.India rotated their bowling resources, using seven bowlers during the innings. Nandani emerged as the pick of the attack, taking three wickets for 18 runs to break Zimbabwe’s resistance and prevent any late surge.Zimbabwe eventually closed on 124/7, finishing 92 runs short of the target.The victory gave India a 3-0 clean sweep in the three-match series and extended their winning run in women’s T20Is to 11 matches, including their campaigns in the Asia Cup in the UAE and the Asian Games in Japan.The result was also India's biggest home victory by run margin in the format. For Mandhana, it marked an impressive start as permanent captain.
Article Summary: India Women thrash Zimbabwe by 92 runs in third T20I in Raipur. Shafali Verma and Harmanpreet Kaur top scored with 69 and 91 respectively. Nandani Sharma took three wickets for 18 runs to break Zimbabwe’s resistance. Sharne Mayers scored a fighting 60 for Zimbabwe.

JAIPUR: Left-arm spinner Ajay Kookna’s timely twin strikes broke two crucial partnerships to derail a solid Railways recovery, keeping Rajasthan firmly in the driver’s seat on Day Three at the Sawai Man Singh Stadium. Railways finished the day at 305/6, still trailing by 192 runs behind the hosts' massive first-innings total, despite a gritty 73-run (203 balls) resistance from captain Bhargav Merai.After starting the day from 46/1, Railways lost two quick wickets in the opening session to pacers Danish Bhambhu and Akash Singh before mounting a recovery. Merai first partnered with Eshaan Goyal (64 off 164) to put together 98 runs.Kookna provided the much-needed first breakthrough after lunch by trapping Goyal lbw, ending their threatening stand. Following this, Merai found another fluent ally in Ravi Singh (53 off 75).Explaining the tactical shift after the break, Kookna pointed out that while they initially expected the pitch to offer help, it did not, so the target was simply to restrict runs by hitting consistent areas. “As the ball gets older, it stops turning, so the new ball helped us break the partnership," he said after the day’s play.The Railways’ pair frustrated the hosts with an 83-run alliance, before Kookna halted their momentum in the final session with his second decisive strike of the day, having the Railways skipper stumped.Soon after, pacer Chetan Sharma removed Ravi, who was caught behind, to reduce the visitors to 256/6.The Railways skipper conceded that when that partnership broke, the momentum shifted. “Our partnership was very crucial. If I had stayed at the crease, we would surely have had the upper hand,” he said.Refusing to surrender, Zubair Ali (18 not out off 33 balls) and Toufik Mondal (33 not out off 48 balls) stitched together an unbroken lower-order resistance through the rest of the evening. The pair narrowed the deficit, keeping alive hopes of avoiding the follow-on as the match heads into the final day.Merai said that they were originally looking to chase the 497-run total. “I have seen big totals being chased down here, so that was our goal. If we had scored 300 for 4, we could still be in the game, but we lost two extra wickets. Zubair scored 100 last year and won two Player-of-the-Match awards, so we are still hopeful of a good partnership of 100 runs, and then things can change," he said."The pitch has gone slower. There is some patch at the far end, so Kookna will be crucial for them on the last day. If we can deal with him, great,” the Railways captain added.

Article Title: 'Where are the fans?': David Warner fumes over sparse crowds in South Africa-Australia Test series

South Africa-Australia series struggles to draw crowds

The ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia has sparked a debate over the popularity of red-ball cricket, with former Australian opener David Warner expressing disappointment over the lack of spectators at the venues. Despite featuring the world's top two Test teams, the series has struggled to draw sizeable crowds, prompting Warner to question whether the format is thriving.The stands were largely empty during the opening Test at Kingsmead in Durban, while rain further affected attendance during the first two days of the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha. The sparse crowds have raised concerns, particularly given the stature of the contest and its significance for both sides."We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving?" Warner wrote on X."You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic," he added.The series carries considerable significance, with Australia entering as the world's top-ranked Test side and South Africa placed second.It is also Australia's first Test tour of South Africa since the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, while the Proteas are playing their first home Test series as reigning world Test champions.Despite the high-profile nature of the contest, the turnout has been underwhelming. The opening Test, which South Africa lost by 214 runs, attracted just under 20,000 spectators across five days at Kingsmead, less than a fifth of the venue's capacity.
Article Summary: South Africa-Australia series struggles to draw crowds. Former Australian cricketer David Warner questioned the lack of attendance. Article Title: India’s medal storm! 24 medals, five golds as Nishad Kumar, Deepthi Jeevanji shine at Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Nishad Kumar and Deepthi Jeevanji (PTI Photo)

Nishad, Deepthi lead India's golden charge

Shooting, powerlifting and swimming add to the haul

Archery assures five medals; badminton stars reach last four

NEW DELHI: India produced a stunning medal rush on Day 2 of the Asian Para Games 2026, collecting 24 medals, including five golds, as athletics powered the country's campaign in Aichi-Nagoya on Tuesday. Nishad Kumar headlined the action with a second gold in as many days, while Deepthi Jeevanji reaffirmed her continental supremacy with a Games-record triumph.At the end of the day's competition, India occupied sixth place in the standings with 35 medals — nine gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze. Athletics accounted for 20 of India's medals so far, underlining its importance to the country's campaign.Alongside the established stars, emerging athletes also delivered encouraging performances, while archery and badminton provided further reasons for optimism by assuring India of more medals in the coming days.Nishad became only the third Indian to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games after adding the men's high jump T47 title to his long jump gold from Monday. The two-time Paralympic silver medallist cleared 2.04m to establish a new Games record.He joined Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi, who had each won two golds at the 2023 Hangzhou edition.Deepthi set the tone early, winning the women's 400m T20 title in a Games-record time of 56.36 seconds.The 23-year-old from Telangana, a former world champion and Paris Paralympics bronze medallist, secured her second consecutive Asian Para Games gold in the event.The golden run continued with Simran winning the women's 200m T12 title in a Games-record 24.80 seconds. Despite struggling with fatigue and limited vegetarian food options, the Paralympic bronze medallist delivered a commanding performance. Games debutant Tejalben Damor added bronze in the same event with a personal-best 25.23 seconds.Pranav Soorma claimed gold in the men's discus throw combined F51/52/53 event with an Asian-record effort of 11.66m, while compatriot Ram Ratan Singh took silver with 10.35m. Devender Kumar completed India's five-gold haul for the day by winning the men's discus throw F44/64 event.India collected two medals in shooting, with Manish Narwal winning silver in the men's 10m air pistol SH1 event and Shrishti Arora taking bronze in the women's 10m air pistol SH1 competition.Narwal, a Paris 2024 Paralympics silver medallist, shot 233.7 in the final to finish behind South Korea's Jo Jeongdu. His performance also secured India a quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics. India's shooting tally rose to four medals after two days, comprising one gold, two silver and one bronze.In powerlifting, Ashok Kumar Malik won silver in the men's 65kg category with a best lift of 192kg. The 37-year-old from Haryana improved on the bronze he won at the previous edition.Swimming contributed two more bronze medals. Himanshu Nandal, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 5:10.91 to finish third in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. Niranjan Mukundan followed with bronze in the men's 200m individual medley SM7, finishing in 2:57.01.Para table tennis also delivered a landmark performance. Ravi Baby Sahana and Prachi Pandey became the first Indian players to win medals in the standing category at the Asian Para Games. They were joined on the podium by Paralympics medallist Bhavina Patel, Sonalben Patel and Jehan Madan, taking India's haul to five bronze medals in the competition.Bhavina lost to China's Zhang Bian in the Class 4-5 semifinal, while Sonalben went down to South Korea's Jiyu Yoon in Class 3. Sahana lost to China's Mao Jingdian in Class 9, and Prachi was beaten by Iraq's Najlah Al-Dayyeni in Class 6.India's medal tally is set to grow further, with para archery assuring the country of at least five medals through finalists across individual, doubles and mixed-team events.Defending champion Sheetal Devi stormed into the women's compound final after defeating Japan's Shinohara Aya 145-137. Sheetal, who equalled the world record and set a new Asian record in qualification, will face Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah for gold.Games debutant Swati Chaudhary also assured India of at least silver after beating South Korea's Eunhee Lee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal.India's women's compound doubles pair of Sheetal and Payal Nag defeated Thailand's Phannibha Srathongmaew and Wasana Khuthawisap 151-135 to reach the gold-medal match. Pooja and Bhawna advanced to the women's recurve doubles final with a 6-2 win over Iran's Mohadeseh Babahabib and Rahimi Ghahderijani Somayeh. Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi also progressed to the men's recurve doubles final after edging South Korea 5-4.The recurve mixed team of Harvinder and Bhawna defeated Thailand 6-0 to reach the semifinals, while Sheetal and Toman Kumar advanced in compound mixed team after beating Japan 154-147.Badminton also guaranteed India more medals. World champion Pramod Bhagat defeated Japan's Daisuke Fujihara 21-12, 21-10 to reach the men's singles SL3 semifinals, extending his record of podium finishes at the Para Asiad to five consecutive editions. He will face South Korea's Lee Seunghu on Thursday.Paralympic gold medallist Kumar Nitesh also advanced to the last four after beating compatriot Vikram Kumar 21-8, 21-8. He will meet Indonesia's Al Muh Imran in the semifinal.With five golds already secured on Tuesday and more medals assured in archery and badminton, India ended Day 2 with momentum firmly on their side as the campaign gathered pace in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India collect 24 medals, including five golds, on Day 2 of the Asian Para Games 2026. Nishad Kumar becomes third Indian to win two golds in a single edition. Deepthi Jeevanji wins Games-record gold in 400m T20 event.

Article Text:
Devender Kumar leads India's historic 1-2-3 finish in men's discus throw (Image: X)

Devender's second-round effort seals gold

Pardeep takes bronze despite longest throw

How the Raza points system works

India enjoy record medal haul on Day 2

India scripted a memorable podium sweep at the Asian Para Games, with Devender Kumar, Rakesh and Pardeep Kumar claiming gold, silver and bronze, respectively, in the men's discus throw F43/F44/F62/F64 final. Devender led the Indian charge with 781 Raza points, while Rakesh finished second with 771 points. Pardeep completed the clean sweep with 669 points, despite recording the longest throw of the competition.Devender secured gold with a best effort of 49.71 metres in his second attempt. After opening with 48.85m, he fouled on his third and fourth throws, managed 45.20m in the fifth, and recorded another foul in his final attempt. His second-round effort ultimately proved decisive.Rakesh claimed silver with 771 points after recording a best throw of 49.35m in his fourth attempt. He began with 47.87m before registering 46.08m in the second round and fouling on his third attempt. Although he could not improve on his fourth-round effort in his final two throws, it was enough to secure second place.Pardeep, competing in the F64 classification, won bronze with 669 points despite producing a personal-best throw of 51.15m in his second attempt.He opened with 46.95m before improving significantly, followed by 50.83m in the third round. His remaining throws measured 46.16m, 48.80m and 47.84m.The event brought together athletes from different classification categories, with the Raza points system determining the final standings. The system adjusts performances into points to account for differences in disability classifications, meaning the longest throw does not necessarily guarantee the highest finish. India's trio made the most of the format to secure all three medals in a commanding display.India enjoyed a landmark outing on Day 2 of the Asian Para Games, securing a record 24 medals across athletics, para table tennis, shooting, powerlifting and swimming. The day's highlights included Nishad Kumar 's gold in the men's high jump T47 with a Games record, Deepthi Jeevanji's gold in the women's 400m T20, and Pranav Soorma's gold in the men's discus throw F51/F52/F53. NEW DELHI: Nishad Kumar scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, winning his second gold medal in as many days to become only the third Indian to claim two golds in a single edition of the continental para-sport showpiece.The two-time Paralympic silver medallist clinched the men's high jump T47 title with a Games-record effort of 2.04m in Aichi-Nagoya, a day after winning gold in the men's long jump T47 event with a best effort of 7.11m.Nishad's double-gold performance puts him in an elite club alongside Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi, who had both won two gold medals at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China.Dhama won the men's 5000m T11 and 1500m T11 titles, while Sheetal struck gold in the women's individual compound open and mixed team compound open events.Known primarily for his high-jump exploits, Nishad demonstrated his versatility by adding the long jump crown to his collection before returning to his speciality on Tuesday.His 2.04m clearance secured the gold and established a new Games record in the men's high jump T47 category, which is meant for athletes with upper-limb impairments.The Indian's latest triumph adds to an impressive career that includes a silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics and a world championship gold in the high jump.Nishad's journey has been marked by extraordinary resilience. His right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm in Amb, Himachal Pradesh, when he was just six years old.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had congratulated Nishad after his long jump gold on Monday, highlighting the significance of winning the event on his Asian Para Games debut."Very proud of Nishad Kumar on winning Gold in the Men’s Long Jump T47 event at the Asian Para Games 2026 with an outstanding jump. NEW DELHI: India's Simran scripted a golden comeback at the Asian Para Games 2026, setting a new Games record to win the women's 200m T12 title with her new guide Shivam, while compatriot Tejalben Damor added a bronze to complete a memorable outing for the country on Tuesday.The 26-year-old Simran clocked 24.80 seconds to claim her maiden gold at the continental showpiece, finishing ahead of Iran's Hajar Safarzadeh, who took silver in 25.02 seconds. NEW DELHI: India continued to swell their medal tally at the Asian Para Games 2026 as Pranav Soorma and Ram Ratan Singh secured a memorable one-two finish in the men's discus throw combined F51/52/53 event on Tuesday, with Soorma setting a new Asian record to clinch gold.The 32-year-old Soorma produced a best throw of 11.66m in his fourth attempt to take the top spot, while compatriot Singh, 31, claimed silver with an effort of 10.35m in his second attempt. Both athletes compete in the F51 classification.The result added another gold and silver to India's growing medal haul at the continental para-sport event in Aichi-Nagoya, with the Indian duo delivering a standout performance in the field.Soorma continued his impressive run at the Asian Para Games after winning gold in the men's club throw F51 event at the previous edition in China. His record-breaking effort in the discus throw further underlined his credentials as one of India's leading para-athletes.Singh complemented his compatriot's performance with a silver-winning throw, ensuring India occupied the top two positions in the event.Iran's Alireza Hemami, competing in the F53 classification, finished with the bronze medal after recording a throw of 20.20m in the fourth round.Although Hemami registered a longer distance than both Indian athletes, he finished third because the combined event's standings were determined using the Raza Point System.The system adjusts performances according to athletes' disability classifications, converting results into standardised points to allow fair comparisons between competitors with different levels of impairment.The F51 classification includes athletes with significant limitations in trunk, leg and hand movement, alongside varying restrictions in arm function. Events may combine athletes from different classifications when participation numbers are limited.The F51-F57 categories cover seated throwing events for athletes with various lower-body impairments, limb deficiencies and limitations in muscle power or range of movement.

A sage plant discovered in the Peruvian Andes has become the sixth species named after Lionel Messi , extending a record already shared by a lizard, spider, fossil brachiopod, condor and fungus. The newly describedcarries Argentina’s familiar blue and white colours in its flowers, but the tribute comes with a troubling detail: researchers have classified the plant as endangered.is a sage species endemic to the Andes of central and southern Peru, where it grows on rocky, arid slopes between 2,000 and 2,400 metres above sea level. It belongs to the mint family, Lamiaceae, which includes plants associated with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties.The plant can grow to approximately 1.5 metres tall, with pale blue and white flowers that resemble Argentina’s national colours. Those colours make the choice of namesake especially fitting for a footballer who represented his country across a career spanning more than two decades.The name follows botanical naming conventions, which often adapt a person’s surname into Latin. The ending “i” indicates possession, socan be understood as “Messi’s sage”.The species was described by researchers led by Paul Gonzales of the Natural History Museum at the National University of San Marcos, alongside Argentine researcher Rolando Uria and biologist Jean Capcha-Ramos of Huarango Nature. Their study appeared in the October edition of the botanical journalThe plant’s restricted range and endangered classification give the discovery significance beyond its unusual celebrity namesake. Its name may draw attention to the species, but its survival depends on protecting the mountain habitat where it grows.In May 2024, Guinness World Records recognised Messi as the footballer with the most species named after him, recording five at the time.now brings that total to six.The names span living animals, prehistoric fossils, fungi and now a flowering plant. The fossil condor and brachiopod also show that the honour is not limited to species alive today.Messi’s record is unusual, although he is not the only footballer whose name has entered scientific classification. Diego Maradona has been associated with four named organisms, but one, the fairy wasp, was later found to be the same species as an earlier-named wasp and is therefore no longer considered valid.Messi’s name has reached science through a series of researchers choosing to recognise his influence, rather than through any single award or official campaign. The latest example connects his sporting identity directly with Argentina’s colours, even though the plant itself grows across the border in Peru.The tribute also arrives after a remarkable international career. Messi made his senior Argentina debut against Hungary on 17 August 2005, briefly retired from international football in 2016, then returned to lead the team through its major successes.He captained Argentina to Copa América titles in 2021 and 2024 and the 2022 World Cup triumph in Qatar. Messi has made 208 appearances and scored 126 goals for Argentina, winning the Ballon d’Or eight times. He scored in Argentina’s 3-0 victory over Benin in his final international match earlier this month. Now 39, he continues his club career with Inter Miami and has also been nominated among the 30 contenders for the 2026 Ballon d’Or.The practice of naming newly described organisms after footballers goes back further than Messi’s record. In December 2009, researchers named 12 newly described microcaddisfly species after members of Brazil’s 1958 World Cup-winning team, including Pelé, whose name was given toMaradona’s scientific namesakes include a fossil damselfly, a parasitic fluke and a sea snail, alongside the wasp later found not to be a distinct species.For Messi, the new sage adds another entry to a record already recognised by Guinness, while also drawing attention to a plant whose future is less secure than the footballer’s place in the sport’s history. The sixth namesake may be a small botanical discovery, but it carries both a tribute and a reminder of the biodiversity researchers are still identifying.
Article Summary: Messi’s latest botanical honour takes his Guinness World Records tally to six species, including animals, fossils and fungi. A sage plant discovered in the Peruvian Andes has become the sixth species named after Lionel Messi, extending a record already shared by a lizard, spider, fossil brachiopod, condor and fungus.
